questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get familiar with the Norwegians institutions, as i will probably be working in norway in the future

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great opportunies in courses and good professors. The curriculum is also exciting and rewarding.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. The UiO website is easy to navigate and very informative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I reacieved assistance upon request, when i adressed the Institute of Psychology by mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall the information you need is easily available online and i didnt need help upon arrival. I needed some help in applying for courses, and recieved support through mail.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I own an apartment in Oslo in which i stayed during the mobility. It is easy to find accomodation in Oslo (for example of
finn.no
or
hybel.no
), but its quite expensive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its expensive, and may be hard to find accomodation that doesnt require you to sign a lease for at least one year at a time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be prepared that it will cost to live in Oslo. The best opportunity for students is usually to find a flatmate or a shared appartment with 2-4 other students/people. Unless you are able to get student housing through SiO, but there is a que-system that may not correlate well with an exchange program.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process is easy through studentweb, and its easy to find information about courses on the UiO webpage. However, to be able to take courses in clinical psychology (which is a separate six-year programme at UiO) i had to contact the institute directly and apply for the courses in a separate form.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is easy through studentweb, and its easy to find information about courses on the UiO webpage. However, to be able to take courses in clinical psychology (which is a separate six-year programme at UiO) i had to contact the institute directly and apply for the courses in a separate form.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Fast reply on e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that courses in clinical psychology is separate from the other master courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: High lquality on lectures and curriculum.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master in clinical psycholoy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UiO feels superior to UCPH. High quality and easy to navigate in lectures and information. Teaching is more hands on and feels more relevant to the actual work that we are going to be doing as psychologists.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYC3300 psychopathology 
PSYC4310 Psychological treatment and treatment research 
PSYC4330 Clinical Neuropsychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
PSYC3300 psychopathology 
PSYC4310 Psychological treatment and treatment research 
PSYC4330 Clinical Neuropsychology

These are all very good and relevant. PSYC4330 offers training in reading psychological test profiles and administering neuropsychological teests, whilst PSYC4310 offers an informative, thourough and engaging line of lectures. PSYC3300 is a basic psychopathology course.

questions.answer: City life. Bars and restaurants are expensive. As is alcohol, due to the monopoly (vinmonopolet)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Oslo is a great city with alot of opportunities. Exiting city life, closeness to nature and so on

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gym, choir, student pubs with quiznights

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the Nature. Oslo is close to nature, you can swim in the ocean in the mddle of the city, and go hiking or skiin right from your home. A lot of great hiking and skiing possibilities are also reachable with the metro.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Use the Nature. Oslo is close to nature, you can swim in the ocean in the mddle of the city, and go hiking or skiin right from your home. A lot of great hiking and skiing possibilities are also reachable with the metro. 

Oslo is a great food-city. Although expensive i would reccomend trying some of the many great restaurants from all over the world.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, similar to denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask to join facebook groups of fellow students on the courses. The often have facebook groups for each of the classes where they post about atudent activites and parties.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The prices on city life andrestaurants.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nature, food, art exhibitions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Althoug a lot of the lectures are not manditory, it is very high quality and i reccomend attending 
2. Blindern (the university campus) is a bit remote from the city center. The city iffers city bikes, ehere you can purchase seasonali tickets, pick up a bike anywhere and deliver it all over the city. 
3. As a student you get good prices at the gym. The offer group sessions included in the price (around 130 DDK a month)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: High quality lectures and professors.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prices, Oslo is an expensive city. Accomodation, food, city life and transportation is pricy compared to other european cities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
